tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session navigated to an order view, clicked Reorder, reached the Create New Order page with items pre-populated, selected the customer, and prepared to submit the order. The final Submit Order click was not executed due to blocking UI (modals/loading overlays) and lack of a visible form_key in the static dump. The Reorder action is typically reachable by a simple URL pattern containing the internal order_id.

Task Definition:
- Purpose: Create a new admin order using items and customer data from an existing Magento order identified by the internal order_id. The tool should perform deterministic navigation to the reorder endpoint, validate the Create Order page state (form_key, totals, email checkbox), handle blocking UI conservatively, and click the bottom 'Submit Order' control to finalize the order, returning the resulting page content for verification.

Action Plan (detailed to-do list):
1) Navigate to the reorder URL for the provided order_id to trigger Magento's reorder flow. This avoids brittle header/button clicks. 2) Inspect the Create Order page to capture form_key, order totals, and the Email Order Confirmation control and to detect any blocking overlays or modals. 3) If blocking modals exist, attempt to close them politely (Cancel/Close) and, if necessary, hide/remove overlays (loading mask). 4) Ensure the Email Order Confirmation checkbox is in the desired state. 5) Locate the bottom-most 'Submit Order' control using XPath text-based match and click it. 6) Capture the resulting page and detect success (order created) and extract the new order id/URL.

Variable Identification (inputs):
- admin_base_url (required): host/protocol for admin URLs (derived from recorded URLs). 
- order_id (required): internal order_id used in admin reorder URLs. 
- send_order_confirmation (optional): whether to check the email checkbox before submit. 
- close_modals (optional): whether to attempt closing/dismissing blocking modals. 
- wait_timeout (optional): how long to wait for overlays or redirects.

Step Optimization:
- Replace UI click sequence that finds the Reorder button in the order view with direct navigation to the canonical reorder URL (faster and deterministic): {admin_base_url}/index.php/admin/sales_order/reorder/order_id/{order_id}/. 
- Use a single agentic DOM step to handle dynamic runtime tasks (closing modals, toggling checkbox, finding and clicking the bottom Submit Order). This keeps steps deterministic and avoids brittle element-index reliance. 
- Prefer XPath-based text matches for the Submit button (exact 'Submit Order' match) and select the last visible occurrence to target the bottom control reliably. 
- Only include steps essential to the task: navigate to reorder, inspect, handle blockers, set checkbox, click submit, return result. Do not add optional filtering/sorting steps.

Determinism & Safety notes:
- The tool assumes an authenticated admin session exists in the browser context where it runs. It does not perform login steps. 
- Because some installations disable form_key validation for checkout or hide the token dynamically, the tool attempts to detect input[name='form_key'] at runtime and logs it; if missing but required server-side, the submit will fail—caller should verify form_key presence in that case. 
- Modal dismissal is conservative: prefer clicking Cancel/Close; DOM removal is only used as a fallback. 

This tool implements the minimal, essential sequence to create an order via Magento's re-order mechanism while handling the dynamic behaviors recorded in the session.
name: create_order_from_existing_order
description: Create a new admin order by re-ordering an existing order. The tool navigates to the Magento admin reorder URL for the provided order_id, confirms the Create Order page loaded, closes blocking modals/overlays, optionally toggles the Email Order Confirmation checkbox, and clicks the bottom 'Submit Order' control. It returns the page content after submission so the caller can confirm the new order was created.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the admin reorder endpoint for the specified internal order_id. Magento's reorder controller usually redirects to the Create Order (/admin/sales_order_create/) page with items pre-populated.
Collect page-level evidence required to safely submit the order (form_key, totals, email checkbox presence/state, visible modals/overlays).
steps.goal: Confirm the Create Order page loaded and capture presence/value of hidden form_key, order totals (subtotal/grand total), and presence of an 'Email Order Confirmation' checkbox. Also detect visible blocking UI (Configure Product modal or loading-mask).

steps.description: Performs DOM-aware operations requiring runtime inspection and conservative modal handling. This step executes JS-driven actions that can't be guaranteed by static selectors alone.
steps.task: On the live Create Order page (result of reorder): 1) If {close_modals} is true, politely dismiss any visible 'Configure Product' or popup-window by clicking a Cancel/Close button (fallback: hide/remove the modal). 2) Wait for any loading mask (#loading-mask or .loading-mask) to disappear; if it remains, hide it. 3) Locate the 'Email Order Confirmation' checkbox by label proximity or known names; if found, set its .checked state to {send_order_confirmation} (if provided) or true by default. 4) Locate the bottom (last visible) 'Submit Order' control using XPath that finds button/input/a with exact text/value 'Submit Order' and picks the last visible match. 5) Click the bottom 'Submit Order' (dispatch real mouse events if necessary). 6) Wait for navigation or loading mask change and capture the resulting page URL and contents. Return any detected new order confirmation text or resulting order view URL.

steps.description: Allow the UI to settle after the agent actions and the submit click (wait for redirects/Ajax to start).
Capture and return the resulting page content so the caller can verify that the new order was created and obtain its identifier.
steps.goal: After submit: extract any success/error messages, detect 'The order has been created.' message, capture resulting order view URL (if redirected) and any new order increment id or internal id present on the page.

input_schema.name: admin_base_url
input_schema.description: Base URL of the Magento admin interface (protocol + host). Example: "http://dockerized-magento.local". Do not include a trailing slash.

input_schema.name: order_id
input_schema.description: Internal Magento order_id used in admin controller URLs (numeric). Example: "204" for /admin/sales_order/view/order_id/204/.

input_schema.name: send_order_confirmation
input_schema.description: If true, ensure the 'Email Order Confirmation' checkbox is checked before submitting the order. Default: true.

input_schema.name: close_modals
input_schema.description: If true, attempt to close blocking modals (e.g. 'Configure Product') before final submit. Default: true.

input_schema.name: wait_timeout
input_schema.description: How many seconds to wait for page loads/overlays to clear before failing. Default: 15.
